text.en:
Divya made two rubber stamps from the same mould. When she pressed them on paper one over the other, the prints matched exactly.
"They are twins," she said. "In maths we call such shapes congruent."

Two shapes are congruent if one fits exactly over the other, matching in size and shape. They may be turned, flipped or slid. Matching sides and angles are called corresponding parts and they are equal.
Two triangles are congruent if three sides of one equal the three sides of the other (SSS). They are also congruent if two sides and the angle between them are equal (SAS), or if two angles and the side between them are equal (ASA).
Congruence is useful in making identical parts for machines, tiles and buildings. Shapes with the same shape but different sizes are not congruent.
Two shapes are congruent if one fits exactly over the other.
Matching sides and angles are equal.
Triangles are congruent if three sides are equal, or two sides and the angle between them are equal.
Same shape but different size is not congruent.

problem.en: Triangle ABC has sides 3, 4, 5 cm and triangle PQR has sides 5, 3, 4 cm. Are they congruent?

text.en: Write the sides in order: 3, 4, 5 and 3, 4, 5.
All three sides of one equal the three sides of the other.

why.en: The order of naming does not matter.

prompt.en: A friend says all squares are congruent. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: Squares can have different side lengths.
Only squares of the same side are congruent.

points.en: Congruent shapes match exactly in size and shape.
Triangles: SSS, SAS and ASA tests.
Same shape but different size is not congruent.
